claim_text: The Legislature says it identified a cybersecurity incident affecting its IT systems on Nov 19
summary: The House of Delegates' communications director said: 'On November 19, 2026, the West Virginia Legislature identified a cybersecurity incident affecting its information technology systems.'
detail: She said teams immediately took steps to contain the incident and began an investigation with outside cybersecurity specialists. The Record, WV MetroNews and The Dominion Post each carry the statement.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three outlets quote the Legislature's spokesperson saying it identified a cybersecurity incident.
notes: This confirms what the Legislature said; it has not used the word cyberattack or said that anyone got in.

claim_text: News outlets report it as a cyberattack
summary: The Record says the Legislature is responding to a cyberattack that took down its website; it says the spokesperson told it the attack started Thursday and continued into Friday. The Dominion Post says a spokesperson confirmed the attack.
detail: The Legislature's own quoted words are 'cybersecurity incident'. The outlets' description of an attack has not been confirmed by any official in words we read.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both outlets describe a cyberattack and attribute its confirmation to the spokesperson.

claim_text: An internal memo described unusual activity identified as a possible ransomware attack
summary: The Dominion Post, citing an internal memo to lawmakers, says IT staff noticed unusual activity on internal systems on Thursday morning, Nov 19, identified as a possible ransomware attack, and shut down systems and remote access.
detail: The memo has not been published, and no official has used the word ransomware on the record in anything we read.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Dominion Post describes the memo's account.

claim_text: Whether it was ransomware has not been confirmed
summary: The spokesperson did not answer The Record's follow-up questions on whether it was a ransomware attack.
detail: The memo's 'possible ransomware attack' (c003) is the only mention of ransomware.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The Record says the question went unanswered.

claim_text: The Legislature disabled access to some IT systems and its website went down
summary: The spokesperson said access to certain Legislature IT systems has been temporarily disabled. The Record says the attack took down the Legislature's website.
detail: The Dominion Post, citing the memo, says the shutdown affected shared workstations and sign-ins for email and productivity tools, and that some systems remained offline on Friday afternoon, Nov 20, though work continued as normal.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The spokesperson's statement in three outlets says systems were disabled; The Record reports the website down.
notes: Status as of Nov 20; see c010.

claim_text: Outside specialists, the state Office of Technology and the West Virginia Fusion Center are involved
summary: The Dominion Post says the memo names a cybersecurity law firm, a forensic firm and a ransomware recovery firm, and says the state Office of Technology and the West Virginia Fusion Center are also involved.
detail: The spokesperson's statement confirms only that outside cybersecurity specialists are helping.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Dominion Post describes the memo; The Record quotes the statement on outside specialists.
notes: The individual attorney named in the article is left out.

claim_text: The Legislature says the incident appears limited to its own systems
summary: The spokesperson said: 'based on what we know so far, the incident appears to be limited to the Legislature's computer systems. We have no evidence showing that other state agencies or offices are affected.'
label: Reported
notes: The Legislature's word alone, so Reported.

claim_text: Whether any sensitive information was accessed is not known
summary: The memo, as quoted by The Dominion Post: 'The review is ongoing, and no conclusions have been reached yet.' If sensitive information is involved, it says, the Legislature will meet any notification obligations.
detail: The spokesperson said relevant findings will be shared 'as soon as it is appropriate to do so.'
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source says whether data was taken.

claim_text: No group has claimed the attack in anything we read
summary: None of the outlets reports a claim of responsibility or names an attacker.
detail: We did not open leak or dark-web sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources names an attacker.

claim_text: Whether the systems and website are back is not known
summary: The latest reports, from Nov 20, say some systems were still offline. We found no report since then saying whether the website or the other systems are back.
detail: The Legislature's website did not load when we tried it on Nov 25 (a connection failure, then a 503 error). We do not take that as proof either way.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source after Nov 20 describes the systems' status.
notes: Re-check the Legislature's website and local outlets on every run.
